title: Autonomous AI Proof of the Cycle Double Cover Conjecture
whyItMatters: Settled one of graph theory’s most celebrated 50-year-old open conjectures (Szekeres 1973 / Seymour 1979); independently verified and published on arXiv by Jim Geelen and Sang-il Oum.
summary: OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra produced a complete proof of the Cycle Double Cover Conjecture—stating that every bridgeless graph admits a collection of cycles covering every edge exactly twice. Within a week, leading graph theorists Jim Geelen (Waterloo) and Sang-il Oum (IBS) independently checked the proof and posted streamlined human-verified expositions on arXiv confirming its correctness.
technicalHighlights: Resolved a flagship Wikipedia-listed open problem in structural graph theory open since the 1970s.
Independently verified within days by top graph theorists Jim Geelen (arXiv:2607.15399) and Sang-il Oum (arXiv:2607.16356).
Produced without Lean formalization, showing frontier reasoning models could deliver clean, human-refereeable graph theory proofs.
caveats: Not formalized in Lean at release (owing to sparse graph-theory libraries in Mathlib); formal journal refereeing is still in progress following specialist confirmations.

scoreRationale.foundational: Resolved one of the top central conjectures in structural graph theory, open for over half a century.
scoreRationale.ripple: Directly impacts cycle decompositions, nowhere-zero flows, and graph embedding theory.
scoreRationale.verification: Independently checked and re-derived in two separate arXiv expositions by leading graph theorists.
scoreRationale.velocity: Demonstrated that multi-agent frontier models can crack famous 50-year-old problems in natural language.
